dossier.scp_unleashed.140.title: Chronicle of the Daevites
dossier.scp_unleashed.140.caption: SCP-140 at intake, beside its evidence tag. It opened twice during the photograph.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-140 is to be kept in a storage container in a secure wing, well away from armouries, training grounds and holding cells. **No violence of any kind is permitted near SCP-140.** Personnel hurt anywhere in the wing are to be moved away from it at once.

SCP-140 may be read only with written authorisation. Readers are to note any page that has changed since their last visit. **No attempt is ever to be made to complete it. Its final pages must never be written.**

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-140 is a heavy book bound in red leather, with corners and a framed title plate of aged brass. Whatever was engraved on the plate has worn away. Most of its pages were blank when it was recovered.

SCP-140 writes itself. When living things are hurt near it, dark crimson ink seeps into its pages, a little at a time, until another page of a history is complete: the chronicle of the Daevites, a conquering people found in no other record.

Each page describes a place of theirs, and once a page is written, that place can be found in the world, standing as though it had always been there. Most are ruins. Later pages have taken far more to write than the first.
SCP-140 opens by itself when a person comes near, and closes again when it is left alone.

page.title: Addendum 140-1: Incident Log
text: Incident 140-02: a sparring match was held in the room where SCP-140 was kept. By evening a page had been written describing a burned watchtower. A burned watchtower was later found where the page said it would be.
Incident 140-06: a wounded agent was carried past SCP-140. The book opened as he passed. %rHe reports that he heard a quill.%r
Incident 140-09: a reader found the newest page still wet. The page after it was blank. %rFor a moment, it was not.%r

page.title: Addendum 140-2: The Later Pages
page.text: Near its end the chronicle changes from a history into a foretelling. **Its final pages describe a return.** Every test that would bring those pages closer is forbidden.

page.title: Addendum 140-3: Provenance
page.text: SCP-140 has no recovery record. It was handed to a reader of this file by the individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects, who held it at arm's length the whole time. See field notes.

SCP-140 is a red-bound chronicle of a conquering people, the Daevites. Use it to read; sneak and use it on a surface to lay it down.
It writes itself. Violence near it seeps onto its pages, and what it writes can be found in the world.
It cannot be crafted or destroyed. The SCP-140 dossier brings it; a stranger in Foundation dress hands it over. It fits in a storage container.

gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.1.title: The First Flame
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.1.text: Before there were banners, there was a single flame. It burned in a stone bowl beside the old salt road, and no traveller could say who had lit it. The first Daevites were herders and wanderers who gathered at its warmth through a long and bitter winter. They fed it cedar and oaths, and the flame grew red as rubies. When spring came they would not leave it. They raised a shrine of fitted stone about the brazier and swore that wherever the flame was carried, the world would bow. Here this chronicle begins.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.2.title: The Oath of Ash
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.2.text: In the second year the elders raised nine stones in a ring and lit a great fire at its heart. Each who would be counted among the Daevites walked through the smoke and pressed a palm of ash upon the nearest stone. So the Oath of Ash was sworn: to serve the flame, to spare no rival, and to kneel to no crown but the one the flame would choose. Those who refused were driven into the hills. The ring still stands, though the fire is long cold, and the ash marks have never faded.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.3.title: The Red Banner Raised
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.3.text: The weavers dyed a great cloth in madder and cinnabar until it was as red as the flame, and hung it from a pole of black oak. Beneath it the Daevites gathered their first war host, three hundred strong, and heaped a cairn with one stone for every rival tribe they meant to break. When the cairn stood taller than a man, they marched. The banner went before them, and the dust of their passing dimmed the sun. Wherever it was planted, no other flag was suffered to fly.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.4.title: The Taming of the Plains
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.4.text: The horse lords of the eastern plains mocked the Daevites as slow folk of the stone. They did not mock for long. In a single summer the red host scattered their herds, burned their summer camps and took their chieftains as hostages. Upon the widest plain the victors raised an obelisk of red stone, carved from foot to tip with the triumphs of that season: horses bridled, spears gathered, chieftains bowed. Ever after, the plains paid tribute in horses and grain, and called the Daevites masters.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.5.title: The First Overseer
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.5.text: Among the Daevites lived a hermit named Ashiru, who sat upon a platform of stone above the plains and gazed into the flame for forty days without food. On the forty-first day he rose from the stones and did not touch the ground again. He drifted in his red robe like smoke on a still evening, and wounds closed beneath his hands. Ashiru taught others the stillness of the flame, and they became the first overseers: healers of the host, keepers of the rites and casters of burning words.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.6.title: The Burning of the River Towns
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.6.text: The river towns grew fat on trade and trusted their timber walls. The Daevites came at night with torches and pitch. Overseers drifted above the palisades, calling fire down upon the watchtowers, and the towns woke to find their roofs aflame. By dawn the river ran grey with ash. The merchants who remained knelt upon the muddy banks and swore the Oath of Ash. Their boats and their silver passed to the red host, and from that day the river road belonged to the Daevites.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.7.title: The Spear-Hosts March
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.7.text: Now the Daevites forged their warriors into spear-hosts, each a thousand strong, drilled until they moved as one creature with a thousand bright teeth. Their camps were laid out in perfect rows, the tents dyed red, the cooking fires set in lines like the stars of a constellation. They marched by day and sang by night, and their singing reached the next valley before they did. Many foes laid down their arms at that sound alone. Those who did not met a wall of spears.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.8.title: The Breaking of the Hill Clans
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.8.text: The hill clans had sheltered the oathbreakers driven out in the second year, and the Daevites had not forgotten. The clans fought from crag and cave, and for a whole season the red banner could not climb. Then the overseers taught the spear-hosts to march by night with veiled lanterns. The clans woke to find red barracks raised upon their own high ground. One by one their strongholds fell silent, and the oathbreakers' names were struck from every stone.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.9.title: The Bridge of Nine Days
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.9.text: A great river barred the way west, too deep to ford and too wide for any bridge then known. Daevite builders sank piers of red stone into its bed while archers held the near bank. The foes upon the far shore threw down every span the builders raised, and every span was raised again. For nine days and nine nights the work went on beneath arrows and fire. On the tenth morning the host crossed over, and a gatehouse was built at the bridge's end so that no army might cross it against them.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.10.title: The Armory of Brass
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.10.text: With the western mines in their hands, the Daevites learned to work brass and red bronze. In a hall cut deep into a hillside they gathered their smiths and their finest arms: spears with leaf-shaped blades, helms crested in crimson horsehair, shields faced with brass that threw the sun into their enemies' eyes. The overseers sealed the doors with words of binding, so that none but a sworn Daevite could open them. Much of that armory lies buried still, waiting for hands that remember the oath.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.11.title: The Field of Broken Spears
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.11.text: Seven kingdoms of the west made common cause and met the Daevites upon a wide field beneath a burning sky. The armies were so many that the dust of their marching hid the mountains. From dawn until dusk the battle swayed, and the overseers wove fire above the lines until the grass itself was burning. When the smoke lifted, the field was strewn with broken spears, and the banners of the seven kingdoms lay trampled in the ash. The red banner alone stood upright.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.12.title: The Ash Road
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.12.text: To bind their lands together, the Daevites paved a road of dark basalt from the first flame to the western sea. Every day's march along it was marked by a waystation, where fresh horses waited and a brazier burned night and day. Couriers bearing the overseers' commands could cross the empire in eleven days. Traders called it the Ash Road for the grey dust that rose from it, and travellers learned that the road was safe for all who bowed at its braziers, and for no one else.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.13.title: The Gate of Seven Kings
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.13.text: Upon the borders of the conquered west the Daevites built a fortress, and its gate was cast from the melted crowns of the seven kings who had fallen upon the Field of Broken Spears. It was poured in a single piece, heavier than a hundred oxen, and its doors were carved with the kneeling likenesses of those kings. It was said that no enemy could pass beneath it without feeling their own knees weaken. The garrison kept watch there for a hundred years, and no army ever came.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.14.title: The Vault of Tribute
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.14.text: Tribute flowed along the Ash Road from every conquered land: grain and horses, cedar and salt, silver and gemstones, rare dyes and rarer books. To hold it all, the Daevites cut a vault deep beneath the earth and lined it with stone and brass. Its corridors were guarded by snares of the overseers' devising, and its doors would open only at the command of the flame. The treasurers counted the wealth of the empire there each spring, and each spring the count was greater.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.15.title: The Tower of Whispers
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.15.text: The overseers grew in number and in power, and they raised a tower of red stone where they could gather apart from the world. Its upper rooms had no stairs, for the overseers floated between them. There they taught the arts of healing and of burning, and listened to the whispers that rose from the flame. Some said the whispers were the voice of something greater than the flame, something that waited and grew. The overseers did not say. They only listened, and they wrote.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.16.title: The Colossus of Victory
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.16.text: To mark a hundred years since the first flame, the Daevites carved a colossus taller than any tower. It showed a warrior of the empire with a spear raised toward the sunrise, its face turned to the conquered lands so that all might see it and remember. Its armour was painted red and its spear point was gilded, so that it caught the first light of every morning. Pilgrims came from every province to stand in its shadow. It is said that it fell only when the empire fell.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.17.title: The Siege of the White City
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.17.text: One city refused the oath: a city of white walls upon a white cliff, whose people believed no army could reach them. The Daevites built siege engines of a size never seen before, towers that walked and great arms that hurled burning stones. For two years they ringed the city with earthworks and fire. In the third spring the white walls cracked, and the spear-hosts poured through the breach. The city was renamed for the red banner, and its white stones were carried away to pave the Ash Road.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.18.title: The Hall of the Knights
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.18.text: From the bravest of the spear-hosts the Daevites chose an order of knights, sworn to the flame above all else. They wore armour of red-lacquered plate and fought with long spears and broad swords, and no knight ever retreated while the banner stood. In their hall the knights kept vigil before each campaign, kneeling in rows before the braziers through the long night. Their names were carved upon the pillars, and a name was cut away only if its bearer broke the oath.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.19.title: The Red Scriptorium
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.19.text: The overseers built a scriptorium to keep the memory of the empire, and there this chronicle was first bound in red leather and brass. Its scribes wrote with ink ground from cinnabar and mixed with ash from the first flame. It was said the ink never truly dried, and that the pages drank it slowly, as dry ground drinks rain. The scribes recorded every victory and every vow. In later years they found that the chronicle had begun to write pages by itself, and they did not dare to stop it.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.20.title: The Eternal Braziers
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.20.text: Upon a terrace above the capital the Daevites set a hundred great braziers, each lit from the first flame and never once allowed to go out. Keepers tended them through every hour of the day and night, and a keeper who let a fire die was sent from the empire forever. The terrace could be seen burning from leagues away, so that travellers on the Ash Road were never in darkness. The Daevites said that while the braziers burned, the empire could not fall.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.21.title: The Stair of Heaven
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.21.text: The overseers declared that the flame wished to stand nearer the sky, and so the empire raised a stair of colossal steps, each one taller than a man, climbing toward the clouds. Ten thousand labourers worked upon it for thirty years. At its summit the overseers built a platform of red stone, open to the heavens, where they floated in a ring and chanted through the night. On the night the stair was finished, the stars above the summit burned red, and the overseers fell silent.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.22.title: The Sunken Arena
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.22.text: To keep their warriors sharp in times of peace, the Daevites dug a great arena into the earth, ringed by tiers of red stone. There knights faced one another, captured beasts, and champions of conquered peoples hoping to win their freedom. The crowds roared from the tiers, and overseers floated above the sands to heal the fallen so they might fight again. A champion of the arena was given a red plume and a place among the knights. Few champions of the conquered ever won it.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.23.title: The Observatory of Omens
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.23.text: The overseers watched the heavens from a dome of brass and red stone, reading the turning of the stars for omens of the empire's fate. They charted every comet and every eclipse, and told the rulers of the empire when to march and when to wait. In the last years of their watch they saw a new figure among the stars: six bright points spread like outstretched arms around a burning centre. They named it the Sign of the Six, and they did not speak of it beyond the dome.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.24.title: The Great Hall of Conquest
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.24.text: In the capital rose a great hall where the empire celebrated its triumphs. Its walls were hung with the banners of every conquered people, so many that the oldest lay piled upon the floor like fallen leaves. Long tables ran the length of the hall, and at the feasts of victory the knights sat at them in full armour while overseers floated above with lamps of red glass. At the far end stood an empty throne. The Daevites said that it awaited a ruler worthy of the flame.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.25.title: The Palace of Brass
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.25.text: The overseers foretold that a ruler worthy of the flame would come, and the empire built a palace of brass to receive one. Its domes were sheathed in brass that blazed at sunrise, its doors were cast with scenes of every victory, and its gardens were lit by braziers that burned without fuel. Within, the council of overseers floated in a chamber of mirrors, so that every word spoken there was seen a hundred times. Envoys from distant lands wrote that it shone too brightly to look upon at noon.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.26.title: The Six-Armed Idol
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.26.text: The overseers carved the figure of the one whose whispers they had heard in the flame: a being that floated above the ground with six arms outstretched, calling lightning from the sky, raising thorns of red crystal from the earth and summoning spirits to its side. The idol stood taller than the colossus in a courtyard of red stone. Before it the overseers drew great circles upon the ground and chanted until the circles glowed like embers. They had begun to call their god.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.27.title: The Throne of Ash
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.27.text: The empty throne was carried from the great hall into a chamber of black stone, and its floor was strewn with ash from a hundred braziers. There the overseers poured the power of the empire into their circles, night after night, until the air itself trembled. On the last night the six-armed god descended upon the throne in red fire. When the light faded, it had folded its many arms away and taken the shape of a tall man, and the overseers knelt before their god-king.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.28.title: The Crown Forge
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.28.text: For the god-king the smiths built a forge that burned with fire carried from the first flame itself. Into it they poured gold from every vault and tribute of the empire, and from it they drew a crown so pure that it glowed like an ember. When the god-king set it upon his brow, every brazier in the empire flared at once. He took up a sword as tall as a knight, forged in the same fire, and from that day he led the hosts himself, and no army stood before him.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.29.title: The War Altar
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.29.text: Before every campaign the god-king stood upon a great altar of red stone and raised his sword, and the overseers drew circles of light about him until the ground burned red. The knights who marched from that altar knew neither fear nor weariness. When he wished, the god-king cast off his mortal shape and rose above the battle in his true form, six arms spread wide, calling lightning and crystal thorns and spirits upon his foes. The kingdoms beyond the empire begged for peace, and were refused.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.30.title: The Gate of the God
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.30.text: At the edge of the known world the god-king commanded a gate to be raised, a monument so vast that clouds gathered upon its lintel. Through it, he declared, the empire would march into lands no Daevite had ever seen, and the whole world would bow to the flame. The overseers bound the gate with their circles, and the knights gathered in their thousands upon the plain before it. The god-king raised his sword, and the gate opened upon a road of fire.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.31.title: The Last Procession
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.31.text: The whole empire walked the avenue to the gate: knights in red armour, overseers floating in their robes, and last of all the god-king beneath a canopy of brass, his crown blazing. Statues of every Daevite hero lined the way. The procession passed through the gate and into the light, and the gate closed behind them. One by one the braziers went out. The empire fell silent, and only this chronicle remained, to wait, and to remember.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.32.title: The Return
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.32.text: Hear now what the chronicle foretells. The ink upon these pages is the ink of the old wars, and every page written calls back a little of what was. Enough has been written. In a hidden valley a temple of red stone shall rise, its braziers kindling of themselves. Within it the Daevites shall wake from their long sleep: knights stepping from the shadows in red armour, overseers rising from the floor in their robes. They shall remember the oath, and they shall begin again.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.33.title: The Banners Rise Again
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.33.text: The Daevites shall go out from the temple and raise their banners once more. Upon the hills a war camp shall be pitched in the old manner, its tents dyed red and its fires laid in lines like stars. Travellers shall see the red banners upon the ridges and wonder what kingdom has risen in the night. The overseers shall gather the strength of every Daevite who wakes, and that strength shall grow with each passing day. The world does not know them yet. The world shall learn.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.34.title: The Knights Ride Out
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.34.text: From the camps the knights shall ride out, spears lowered, sweeping the land as they once swept the plains. Another camp shall rise, and then another. Every Daevite who wakes adds to the power of the overseers, and the overseers waste none of it. They store it in their circles, layer upon layer, as their forebears stored tribute in the vault. They are preparing. Those who meet the patrols in the wilds shall carry back the first warnings, and too few shall listen.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.35.title: The God Is Called
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.page.35.text: This is the last page. When it is written, the power stored in the circles shall surge like a river breaking its banks, and the overseers shall gather in the temple to call their god. The six-armed one shall descend in red fire, and when it is struck down it shall rise again as the crowned god-king, sword in hand. Let whoever reads these words understand: this chronicle was never a history. It was always a summons. It should never have been finished.
gui.scp_unleashed.scp140.remains.subject: Its remains lie
The temple wakes
Their banners rise
Their knights muster
The circles burn
